body.name: Data-driven measurement-support cleaning
body.construction:
Fix a positive training-fold-measurable threshold \(\tau_{S,n}\downarrow0\), chosen without the true measurement supports.  Let \(\widehat M_A\) and \(\widehat M_Z\) denote the raw column-stochastic measurement fits.  For all sufficiently large \(n\), so that \(K\tau_{S,n}<1\), define
\[
 \bar M_{A,aj}(x)=
 \frac{\widehat M_{A,aj}(x)\mathbf 1\{\widehat M_{A,aj}(x)>\tau_{S,n}\}}
 {\sum_{b=1}^{K}\widehat M_{A,bj}(x)\mathbf 1\{\widehat M_{A,bj}(x)>\tau_{S,n}\}},
 \qquad
 \bar M_{Z,zj}(x)=
 \frac{\widehat M_{Z,zj}(x)\mathbf 1\{\widehat M_{Z,zj}(x)>\tau_{S,n}\}}
 {\sum_{c=1}^{K}\widehat M_{Z,cj}(x)\mathbf 1\{\widehat M_{Z,cj}(x)>\tau_{S,n}\}}.
\]
These maps take only the raw fitted columns and \(\tau_{S,n}\) as inputs.  Every fitted bridge and every fitted object \(\widehat B,\widehat d,\widehat D,\widehat R,\widehat N,\widehat h,\widehat G,\widehat b_{(\cdot)},\widehat b_U,\widehat Q\) is subsequently recomputed from \((\bar M_A,\bar M_Z)\).  If support sets are supplied as observed design information, imposing those known zeros before applying this same normalization is an optional specialization.
